titulo: Regular pretérito indefinido: The indefinido in -er and -ir, and spelling changes

aula.objetivo: Narrate what happened and is already finished («ayer», «anoche», «el año pasado») with the regular -ar, -er and -ir forms of the pretérito indefinido, get the accent marks right («hablé», «habló»), handle the spelling changes («busqué», «llegué», «empecé», «leyó»), and tell the indefinido apart from the pretérito perfecto.

sessao.titulo: The indefinido in -er and -ir, and spelling changes

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: -er and -ir verbs use the same endings in the indefinido: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. «Comer» becomes «comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron». «Vivir» becomes «viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivisteis, vivieron». STEP 2: the first person «-í» and the third person «-ió» carry an accent: «comí», «comió». STEP 3: in «nosotros», -ir verbs look just like the present («vivimos»), but -er verbs change: present «comemos», indefinido «comimos». STEP 4: watch the third-person ending closely: it's «comió», «vivió» — never anything resembling an English-style reduction. And the plural is «comieron», never «comeron». STEP 5: to keep the sound the same, some -ar verbs change their spelling only in «yo». Verbs ending in «-car» become «-qué» («buscar → busqué»), those in «-gar» become «-gué» («llegar → llegué»), and those in «-zar» become «-cé» («empezar → empecé»). STEP 6: when the stem ends in a vowel, the «i» between two vowels becomes «y» in the third person: «leer → leyó, leyeron». The other forms carry an accent on the «í»: «leí, leíste, leímos, leísteis». «Creer» (creyó) and «oír» (oyó) do the same thing. STEP 7: «salir» is irregular only in the present («salgo»); in the indefinido it's regular: «salí, saliste, salió». STEP 8: a few very common verbs (ser, ir, hacer, tener, decir, ver) are irregular in the indefinido. Those are saved for lesson 20.
blocos.comparacao: English past-tense verbs don't change their ending based on whether the root ends in a vowel or consonant, so the «i → y» spelling shift in «leyó», «creyó», «oyó» has no parallel to lean on — it's simply a Spanish spelling rule to learn on its own. The «-car/-gar/-zar» spelling changes (busqué, llegué, empecé) are the same kind of thing: a pattern that keeps the consonant sound stable in writing, with nothing in English's own spelling system to map it onto.

exemplos.pt: Last night I wrote a long email.

exemplos.ru: Llegué a casa a las nueve.
Ellos vivieron un año en Lima.
exemplos.pt: They lived in Lima for a year.

linhas.motivo: [misto] c + é would sound like «th»; «qu» keeps the «k» sound
[misto] g + é would sound like «h»; «gu» keeps the «g» sound
[misto] z is never written before «e»; it becomes «c»

erros.motivo: In the third person of -er and -ir verbs, the ending is «-ió».
To keep the «g» sound, you write «gu» before the «é».

erros.errado: [misto] El año pasado empezé a estudiar.
erros.certo: [misto] El año pasado empecé a estudiar.
erros.motivo: You never write «z» before «e»; use «c» instead.

blocos.enunciado: Narrate out loud, in at least eight sentences, how your last Sunday went: what you ate and drank, who you wrote to, what time you left and what time you got back. Use «el domingo pasado», «primero», «luego» and «después».
Conjugate «hablar» and «trabajar» in the indefinido, from «yo» to «ellos». Say one sentence with «ayer» and another with «anoche».
